title: Aggrega Core (Provider)
description: The global plugin registrar mapping a rendering engine name to an executable.

version.description: Strict Semantic Versioning of the Provider registrar (e.g., 1.0.0).

description.description: A concise, one-sentence summary of what the entity does.

maintainers.description: List of maintainers who own this entity.

repository.description: The URL to the Git repository where the source files live.

home.description: The URL of this entity's home page, wiki, or documentation.

keywords.description: A list of descriptive keywords for UI discoverability.

deprecated.description: Indicates whether this entity is deprecated and should no longer be used.

spec.description: The plugin URI for the rendering engine and the workloadSchema declaring how this provider materialises a Workload. A Provider whose engine supports workload synthesis renders Recipes that use the synthesized input kind (the workload: block); the standard-library catalog declares a non-empty workloadSchema on such providers as the documented contract. A synthesized-mode Recipe bound to a provider whose engine cannot synthesize halts loudly at render time.

plugin.description: Names the Plugin entity that provides the Wasm rendering engine for this provider, given as a bare catalog identity (`name:version` or `provider/name:version`, e.g. 'helm-renderer:1.0.0'). Resolution is two levels: a provider name resolves to this Provider, this field resolves to the named Plugin entity, and that Plugin's own `plugin` field resolves to the content-addressed Wasm artifact the runtime loads. The value is a bare catalog identity, not a host-prefixed reference — entity resolution matches the pre-version base against the Plugin's `metadata.name`, so a host-prefixed base never matches. Provider render dispatch selects the per-provider engine by provider name and does not yet consume this field; the field carries the resolvable provider-to-renderer link.

workloadSchema.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 documenting how this provider translates the aggrega.ai/v1alpha1 Workload kind into provider-native manifests. When present, the provider supports Recipes that declare a workload: block (synthesized mode) — the compiler synthesizes provider-native manifests via a Go Engine, informed by this schema as documentation/contract. Whether a workload: Recipe is supported is determined by the bound engine's synthesis capability, not by this field's presence: a synthesized-mode Recipe bound to a provider whose engine cannot synthesize halts loudly at render time. The standard-library catalog declares workloadSchema on synthesizing providers as the documented contract, kept in sync with engine capability. Today the field acts as a presence flag (any non-empty body indicates support); the body becomes executable input to Wasm translators in a future iteration.

wellKnownAnnotations.description: Documentation-of-contract: the platform-native well-known annotation keys (the aggrega.ai/ namespace) this provider's rendering engine reads, with the behavior applied when each is absent. Each entry documents one engine-consumed annotation key for catalog readers and the inspect surface. The compiler does not consume this field to gate or branch a build — it is descriptive metadata about the annotations the engine recognises, not an enforcement list, and is distinct from the runtime check that governs binding a value into the reserved namespace. Entries are an ordered list and preserve author order.

key.description: The platform-native well-known annotation key the engine reads (e.g., aggrega.ai/namespace). Sits under the platform-reserved aggrega.ai/ annotation namespace — the engine-read platform directives.

purpose.description: What the annotation controls — the rendering behavior it influences when present.

defaultBehavior.description: The behavior the engine applies when this annotation is absent.
